title: Elevator, 18th Floor
description:
The elevator in a Gangnam office tower stopped.

The button for floor 18 was lit.
The man standing beside {name}. Early forties. Seen on the news a few times.
President of a group subsidiary. The one his grandfather built.

90 seconds.

This man's dress shirt costs more than {name}'s monthly food budget.
The floor this man is going to is the floor {name} is trying to reach — in a different sense.

The elevator hummed upward.

choices.text: Speak first. Made it this far.
choices.result_text:
'Do you come to this building often?' The words came out.

The man glanced over. 'Oh — yes.' Short.

Handed over a card. He took it. Glanced at it.
Floor 18. The doors opened. 'Take care.' Gone.

A week later, {name} sent a text:
'This is the person you met in the elevator...'

Read. No reply.

The card is still in the inside pocket of the wallet.

choices.text: Hand over a card.
choices.result_text:
Held out the card.

He took it. Looked once. Put it in his pocket.
Seemed about to say something. Didn't.

Floor 18. Doors opened.

That was it.

Where that card is now — wonders sometimes.
Thrown away, or passed to someone, or just — forgotten.

choices.text: Pretend not to notice. Different worlds anyway.
choices.result_text:
Head down, phone out.

He looked at his phone too.
90 seconds. Neither said a word.

Floor 18. Doors opened. He walked out.

The back of his shoes was visible for a moment.
Not a scuff on them.

Someone made those shoes.
That person is somewhere, building toward something too.

The elevator doors closed.

title: Health Check Results
description: The results from the annual check-up arrived in the app. Two items flagged 'Caution.' Always tired, yes — but not expecting this. Hand trembled slightly.

choices.text: Read the results. Start with diet.
choices.result_text: Saw the numbers and cleaned out the fridge the same day. Health is something you protect before it breaks.

choices.text: Can't face it. Stuff the printout in a drawer.
choices.result_text: Out of sight, out of mind. The body knows, even if the eyes don't.

choices.text: The test is wrong. Demand a retest.
choices.result_text: Refused to accept it. Went to a different hospital. Denial is a defense mechanism too.

title: Gangnam Open House
description:
Saw a listing and walked in on impulse.

New construction in Gangnam. Open house.

107 sqm. Listed at ₩1,850,000,000.

Seoul was visible through the living room windows.
A staff member gave the pitch. Han River view. School district. Transit links.

The couple standing nearby was nodding.
They were people who could live here.

{name} was standing in that living room.
Feet touching the floor.
That, strangely, felt very real.

choices.text: Ask the staff about financing. Might come back someday.
choices.result_text:
'What's the maximum loan I could get?'

The staff ran the numbers. Income basis, asset basis, rates.

{name} wrote it down.
A cold, clear look at the distance between those numbers and where {name} stands now.

Took a brochure on the way out.
Put it in a desk drawer.

Had a feeling it would be opened again.

choices.text: Just look around. Leave.
choices.result_text:
Walked out.

Heading toward the subway, {name} kept thinking about the living room just left behind.
That floor. That window. That height.

₩1,850,000,000 came out of the building attached.

Got on the subway.
Sat down. Closed eyes.

The feeling of standing in that room stayed for a long time.
The soles of the feet still seemed to remember the floor.

title: Two A.M., the Heart
description:
I woke from sleep.

My chest was pounding.
Not in a steady rhythm.

I had three coffees yesterday. I haven't been sleeping well lately.
Or is something else going on?

It was two in the morning.

choices.text: Book a hospital appointment for tomorrow
choices.result_text:
I found an internal medicine clinic in the app.
Booked it. 10 a.m., the day after tomorrow.
That night, at least, I think I slept a little better.

choices.text: Brush it off as nothing and lie back down
choices.result_text:
I pulled the blanket up.
Closed my eyes.
The pounding stopped twenty minutes later.

choices.text: Search whether I should go to the ER
choices.result_text:
I searched 'heart palpitations ER guidelines.'
Read through the symptom checklist.
None of it applied. Still, I stayed awake for thirty minutes.

title: A Night of Service Memories
description: When life grinds you down, military memories suddenly surface. A senior's face, night guard duty, the hours I endured for no reason. I still don't know whether it made me who I am now, or just wore me down.

choices.text: Pick out only the good memories and look back with gratitude
choices.result_text: I thought of what I learned rather than what was hard. How you edit your memories can change your future.

choices.text: Pour the bottled-up feelings into a journal
choices.result_text: I picked up a pen at dawn. The feelings I poured out went quiet on the paper.

choices.text: Call an old comrade and talk about those days
choices.result_text: I called a comrade I hadn't spoken to in ages. Knowing someone shares the same memories was a comfort.

title: Spiderweb Screen
description:
I slipped on the third step of the stairs.

My phone hit the floor.
There was a sound.

I picked it up. The screen was a spiderweb.
There was an important call coming today.
Or there might have been.

choices.text: Head straight to a repair shop
choices.result_text:
I went to a nearby repair shop.
120,000 won.
Waited an hour. Good as new.

choices.text: Tape it up and just keep using it
choices.result_text:
I found some clear tape.
Stuck it on.
A shard of glass caught the tip of my finger.

choices.text: Swap the device through a secondhand deal
choices.result_text:
I posted it on a used-goods app.
Got a reply within thirty minutes.
Sold it for 70,000 and bought a used phone for 100,000.

choices.text: Check whether insurance covers it
choices.result_text:
I opened the carrier's app.
Turns out I was insured.
Deductible: 30,000 won. Insurance I didn't even remember having.

title: Five Resignation Vlogs
description:
It was a stranger's channel.
The algorithm caught it for me at dawn.

I watched one. Autoplay kicked in. I watched another.
By the fifth video I checked the subscriber count. 81,000.

There was even an ad-revenue receipt video.
{name} has no subscribers.

choices.text: Subscribe and close the window
choices.result_text:
I hit the subscribe button.
The algorithm served up even more videos.
Closing the window took another twenty minutes.

choices.text: Leave one line of encouragement in the comments
choices.result_text:
'Enjoyed watching this.'
After posting it, I looked at my own profile.
Zero subscribers. No uploaded videos.

choices.text: Close the window and sleep
choices.result_text:
Turned it off.
Lay down.
Tomorrow's alarm was set for 6:30.

title: Breaking Policy Announcement
description: A news alert went off. The government announced new finance and real estate policies. I can't tell whether to move before the market reacts, or whether a rash decision will sink me.

choices.text: Analyze the announcement and adjust related assets
choices.result_text: I read the policy text carefully and reworked my portfolio. Reading the news fast is the skill of staying ahead of the market.

choices.text: Tune it out and carry on as usual
choices.result_text: Figuring it wouldn't change anything for me anyway, I ignored it. Whether it was an opportunity, I'll find out later.

choices.text: Dive boldly into the policy-beneficiary stocks
choices.result_text: I read the policy direction and bet boldly. The key is moving before the news breaks.

title: Unsaved Number
description:
An unknown number rang.
Three times.
I hung up.

It came again.

Five seconds of not knowing whether it was spam.

choices.text: Answer it
choices.result_text:
I answered.
It was a college classmate. Five years since we last spoke.
They said 'let's grab a meal.' Unexpected.

choices.text: Hang up first and search the number
choices.result_text:
The search returned 'carrier customer service.'
It wasn't. I sent a text. 'Who is this?' An old acquaintance.

choices.text: Don't answer; confirm by text
choices.result_text:
I sent 'Sorry, who's this?'
No reply.
The next day I saw a 'beware of voice phishing' article.

choices.text: Refuse to answer to the end
choices.result_text:
I didn't answer.
Blocked the number.
Later I learned it had been a college friend's number.

title: AI Face-Reading App
description:
A link popped up in the group chat.
'AI reads your face, everyone try it.'

Friends started posting their results.
Entrepreneur face. Artist face. Office-worker face.

{name} uploaded a photo too.

choices.text: Like the result and save it
choices.result_text:
Result: entrepreneur face.
I took a screenshot.
I don't believe it, but it felt good.

choices.text: Hate the result and do it again
choices.result_text:
It came back office-worker face.
I retook the photo.
The third try was office-worker face too.

choices.text: Share the result in the group chat
choices.result_text:
I posted it.
Friends reacted. 'Yep, that's spot on.'
The group chat buzzed for ten minutes.

title: Haggling on 'No Haggling'
description:
An item I'd listed on the secondhand market.
I clearly wrote it in the last line of the description.
'No haggling, please.'

A message came.
'Could you maybe knock it down to 30,000? ^^'

They must have read it.

choices.text: Politely say the price stands
choices.result_text:
'Sorry, the price isn't negotiable.'
Sent.
Two hours later, someone showed up willing to pay full price.

choices.text: Get annoyed and refuse the deal
choices.result_text:
I replied, 'You saw the read receipt, right?'
They left a bad review.
One star.

choices.text: Counter-haggle in turn
choices.result_text:
'30,000 is too low, but add 20,000 and I'll cover shipping.'
They accepted.
Not a bad outcome.

title: LinkedIn Message
description:
A LinkedIn notification.

'Hello, I'm reaching out after seeing {name}'s profile. Our company is looking for someone like you.'

An HR rep from a company I didn't know.
No salary info.
No way to tell if it was better or worse than my current job.

choices.text: Research the company first
choices.result_text:
I searched the company name.
A two-year-old startup. Thirty employees.
Reviews were mixed. I read them once more.

choices.text: Reply that I'm interested
choices.result_text:
'Hello, could I hear more details?'
Sent.
The next day a video interview offer came.

choices.text: Ignore it and close
choices.result_text:
Turned off the notification.
Closed LinkedIn.
The next day a text came from the same number.

title: A Forgotten Bankbook
description:
While tidying up my banking apps, I found it.

An account I'd opened long ago.
Balance: 47,200 won.

I couldn't even remember the last time I'd looked at it.
Maybe it had been even longer.

choices.text: Transfer it to the investment account
choices.result_text:
Transferred.
47,200 won joined the investment account.
Even small money has its place.

choices.text: Spend it on dinner tonight
choices.result_text:
I went to a barbecue place.
Alone, but it didn't matter.
Ate 47,200 won's worth. For the first time in a while, I was full.

choices.text: Just leave it
choices.result_text:
Closed the app.
Decided to forget it.
If I find it again next time, I'll think about it then.

choices.text: Decide not to touch it for now
choices.result_text:
Opened the bankbook, then closed it.
The 47,200 won will stay where it is.
Tomorrow's {name} can decide.

title: Ex-Boss on the Subway
description:
Subway Line 4.
The doors opened.

I saw who came in.
It was my old team lead.

They saw me too.
Our eyes met.

choices.text: Greet them first
choices.result_text:
'Hello.'
The team lead came closer.
'How've you been lately?' The conversation lasted three stops.

choices.text: Move to another car
choices.result_text:
I slipped into the next car before the doors closed.
Avoided the awkwardness.
I think they saw.

choices.text: Pretend to be on my phone and ignore them
choices.result_text:
I lowered my head.
The screen was off.
They got off at the next station.

title: Card Statement
description:
The statement arrived.

87,000 won more than I expected.
I went through the items one by one.

Two subscriptions. No memory of signing up.
Three online purchases. I remembered buying only one.

The other two, {name} couldn't recall.

choices.text: Check each item and cancel everything
choices.result_text:
I found the subscription services.
Canceled both.
23,000 won saved per month. 276,000 a year.

choices.text: Keep only what I need and clear out the rest
choices.result_text:
One I was using.
One I'd forgotten.
I canceled only the one I'd forgotten.

choices.text: Just pay it this month
choices.result_text:
Paid it.
Decided to sort it out next month.
When next month's statement came, the same items were there.

title: Mail from the Military Manpower Administration
description: An envelope from the Military Manpower Administration was stuck in the mailbox. A white envelope with a red stamp. My heart sank before I even opened it. I knew it was the kind of mail you can't ignore.

choices.text: Read it carefully and respond properly
choices.result_text: I opened the envelope and read it line by line. Better to know and handle it than to let it slide unaware.

choices.text: Put off opening it and miss the deadline
choices.result_text: I kept saying 'I'll open it later' and missed the deadline. I learned you can't ignore mail from the MMA.

choices.text: Look into legal exceptions
choices.result_text: Every rule has exceptions. You have to read the rules to defend your rights.

title: The Meeting Room Door Closed
description:
Right after lunch.

The team lead's voice was low.
'Got a minute?'

We walked down the hall together.
Not a word.
The meeting room door closed.

Those thirty seconds felt strangely long.

choices.text: Listen calmly and ask how to improve
choices.result_text:
I listened.
It was about performance targets.
I asked, 'What would you suggest I do?' It turned into a conversation.

choices.text: Swallow it inside and nod along
choices.result_text:
I nodded.
Managed my expression.
Left the meeting room and went to the bathroom.

choices.text: Push back and state my own view
choices.result_text:
I started with, 'From my side, that part...'
The team lead's face hardened.
It turned into a ten-minute argument.

choices.text: Step away to collect my emotions
choices.result_text:
I needed some air.
Went down the stairwell.
Came back up five minutes later.

title: In Front of Domino's at Gangnam Station
description:
In front of the Domino's at Gangnam Station.

A neatly dressed person approached.
'Excuse me, do you have a moment?'

They held out a business card.
'Would you hear out our business pitch? It'll only take ten minutes.'

choices.text: Decline politely
choices.result_text:
'No thank you.'
I bowed my head and walked past.
Behind me I heard them start in on the next person.

choices.text: Listen for just ten minutes
choices.result_text:
We went to a nearby cafe.
The business model came out.
When the pitch crossed the fifteen-minute mark, I stood up.

choices.text: Film it and post it on SNS
choices.result_text:
I quietly turned on the camera.
Posted it.
A comment read, 'Got got by them too.'

title: Real Estate Regulation Rumor
description:
The real estate community was on fire.

'100% sure there's an announcement this Friday'
'If it's deregulation, buy now'
'If it's tighter rules, time to sell'

The source: a 'friend of a friend.' That friend every community has.

{name}'s portfolio had real-estate-related holdings.

choices.text: Check the rumor's source first
choices.result_text:
I searched for articles.
No official announcement was scheduled.
The community post got edited. 'Some say it's been canceled.'

choices.text: Bet on deregulation and buy
choices.result_text:
I bought in.
Friday came with no announcement at all.
Monday's market was flat.

choices.text: Trim my holdings just in case
choices.result_text:
I sold off a portion.
Friday, deregulation was announced.
The part I sold rose by exactly that much.

title: Instagram Comparison Hell
description: I opened Instagram before bed. A friend posted vacation photos abroad. Another, housewarming photos. Another, news of a promotion. The more I scrolled, the shabbier my own feed looked.

choices.text: Close the app and focus on my own goals
choices.result_text: I stopped scrolling and got to work. Comparison feeds on energy and grows.

choices.text: Wear myself down, blaming myself again and again
choices.result_text: The more I looked at the feed, the smaller I felt. I knew it, and still couldn't stop.

choices.text: Analyze the popular accounts' strategies and copy them
choices.result_text: I turned jealousy into analysis. I'm learning to use envy as motivation.

title: Friend's Phone Screen: +64%
description:
A dinner out.

A friend held out their phone screen.
+64%.

'I bought it last month.'

This friend never used to invest.
{name} set down the beer glass.

choices.text: Ask how they bought in
choices.result_text:
'What is it?'
The friend explained.
{name} nodded along, then pulled out a notepad.

choices.text: Congratulate them sincerely
choices.result_text:
'Man, that's huge.'
We toasted.
On the way home I searched the name of that stock.

choices.text: Drink more beer
choices.result_text:
Took a sip.
Changed the subject.
Decided tonight would just be a drinking night.

choices.text: Copy them and buy in right now
choices.result_text:
Opened the app.
Found the stock.
Bought. The friend said, 'Hey, don't do that.'

title: Weekly Usage Time
description:
A notification popped up on my phone.

'Your weekly screen time report'

{name} tapped it.

Daily average: 5 hours 14 minutes.

It broke it down by category.
YouTube. Stock app. Real estate app. News.
And — search history.

'Average price of a Gangnam apartment'
'Average net worth at 33'
'Minimum monthly living cost in Seoul'

The phone knew what {name} wanted.
In numbers.

choices.text: Decide to cut back. There's time to spend elsewhere.
choices.result_text:
I set an app limit. One hour a day.

Three days later I removed the limit.

Still, just learning something about myself meant something.
Seeing what I want laid out in numbers was strangely honest.

choices.text: Just let it slide. Everyone probably lives like this.
choices.result_text:
Let it slide.

And five minutes later, opened YouTube.
'Average net worth in your 30s is 100 million? Here's the reality.'

The algorithm is always a step ahead.

title: The Whole Country Is Buying Stocks
description:
The group chat came alive.

People who were usually quiet suddenly had a lot to say.
Everyone was posting profit screenshots.

'Made 3% yesterday'
'I really hit it big this time'
'Hey, why aren't you in yet?'

I looked at the KOSPI chart. It kept rising.
The news said 'retail investors at an all-time high.'

That feeling that if you don't ride this wave, you'll be the only one left behind.
Exactly that feeling.

choices.text: Decide to ride it. The chance is now.
choices.result_text:
I put in 3 million won.

The first two days it rose. I thought I'd called it right.
The next week a correction came.

The group chat went quiet.
Nobody posts screenshots of their losses.

FOMO runs both ways.
The fear of buying in and the fear of falling weighed the same.

choices.text: Just watch. This could be the top.
choices.result_text:
I watched.

Three weeks later the chart turned down.
The group chat went quiet.

Maybe I did the right thing. Maybe not.
Had it risen, I'd have said, 'I should've gotten in after all.'

Whatever you choose, there's room for regret.
That was investing.
